kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the printed facts — 4 patterns (two-phase Aδ/C pain, the NSAID-at-transduction station question, the diabetic neuropathic fork, the local-anesthetic two-station span), 4 traps (transduction-vs-transmission, Aδ-vs-C, nociceptive-vs-neuropathic, gabapentinoids-vs-antidepressants by station pair), 3 pivots.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the definitions and the four blocker lists only; the attack structure is a KYP design.

kypExtensions.summary: The plain-word jobs of the four stations (CONVERT / CARRY / TUNE / FEEL) and the fast-lane/slow-lane fiber framing. The page NAMES all four processes but only DEFINES transduction (the TRPV sentence) and transmission (the Aδ/C sentence) — modulation and perception print as bare names with blocker lists, so their one-line glosses, the CONVERT-CARRY-TUNE-FEEL code, and the lane-speed framing are KYP synthesis.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints two mechanism sentences and two bare process names; the station-job layer and the reading protocol (SORT / STATION / LIST / OVERLAP) are KYP's design.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + blocks[3] the steps block + the registry visual's station cards

kypExtensions.summary: The station × drug-class matrix (blocks[2]), the 6·3·4·5 blocker-count spine, and the three-asymmetries callout (blocks[4]) — the printed lists re-sorted by drug class so each drug's station span is visible: local anesthetics transduction+transmission; α2-agonists three stations; gabapentinoids transduction+modulation; NSAIDs/acetaminophen/glucocorticoids transduction-only; opioids transmission+perception; TCAs/SSRIs/SNRIs modulation+perception.
kypExtensions.rationale: The page prints the lists BY STATION; flipping the axis to BY DRUG CLASS is a KYP re-sorting of the same printed facts (every cell sourced from the printed lists, nothing added).

kypExtensions.summary: The osteoarthritis miniCase (a 66-year-old with mechanical two-phase knee pain — sharp Aδ jab then dull C-fiber ache — relieved by naproxen; asked which of the four processes the NSAID blocks) with distractors quoting the transmission, modulation, and perception lists accurately for the wrong stations.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid prints the four lists but never asks the learner to route a drug through them; the vignette, the four options, and the reasoning are KYP's design.
